frozen_decisions_applied: Plan S5 #9: 'Create explicit encrypted NVS namespaces/ownership for Wi-Fi credentials, MQTT credentials/trust references, admin verifier, TLS private key/certificate reference, session seed and manufacturing provisioning records.' -- all six named as NvsNamespaceId entries, in the plan's own listed order, each with encryption_required=true.

Plan S5 #15: 'Classify every eFuse/partition/NVS namespace/key as PRESERVE_ON_FACTORY_RESET, ERASE_ON_FACTORY_RESET or RESET_JOURNAL_ONLY; an unclassified namespace blocks S8 reset implementation.' -- every registry entry carries exactly one NvsResetClassification value, sourced directly from FD-21's own preserve/erase text (quoted verbatim in the header), with the three FD-21 Preserve items that are not NVS namespaces (eFuse/security state, flash/NVS encryption key material, factory GatewayId) explicitly documented as not applicable rather than given a fabricated entry.

This project's established real-tool-grounding discipline (S5's Kconfig work and eFuse-template work both caught real mistakes only once checked against something real) was applied here too: every namespace/key entry is derived from a grepped inventory of this repository's actual hal_nvs_* call sites, including reading config_manager.cpp's build_profile_nvs_key/build_legacy_v2_profile_nvs_key functions directly to get the exact 'rptp_%c%02u'/'cfg_rpt_%c%02u' key-prefix formats rather than guessing from surrounding migration logic.

recon.detail: Grepped every hal_nvs_set_*/hal_nvs_get_* call site across config_manager.cpp, connectivity_manager.cpp, network_manager.cpp, matter_endpoint_registry.cpp, persisted_state_store.cpp, state_persistence_coordinator.cpp, ota_manager.cpp and effect_executor.cpp. Found: wifi_ssid/wifi_password (plaintext Wi-Fi credentials); 8 config_manager scalar/count keys plus 2 dynamic per-profile key-prefix formats spanning 3 schema-version generations (cfg_schema_ver, cfg_cmd_tmo_ms, cfg_cmd_retry, cfg_rpt_cnt2, cfg_rpt_cnt, cfg_rpt_count, cmd_tmo_ms, cmd_retries, rptp_*, cfg_rpt_*); mtep_a/mtep_b (Matter endpoint dual-slot store); dstate_a/dstate_b/core_state_v1 (core device-state dual-slot store plus a legacy single-slot key); ota_dbg_req/ota_dbg_step (OTA debug diagnostics); core_rev (effect-executor test hook). Confirmed hal_identity_get_factory_base_mac() never writes to NVS (eFuse-derived, read every call) and that mqtt_bridge.cpp's legacy_discovery_tombstoned_ flag is RAM-only, never NVS-persisted.

registry_implemented.detail: 12 NvsNamespaceId entries: kWifiCredentials, kMqttCredentials, kAdminVerifier, kTlsIdentity, kSessionSeed, kManufacturingProvisioning (plan #9's six, in the plan's own order); kZigbeeNetworkDeviceReporting, kMatterEndpointState, kCoreDeviceState, kOperationJournalDiagnostics, kLegacyMigrationTombstone (pre-existing data, classified per FD-21); kResetJournal (plan #18's future storage port, classified kResetJournalOnly now so it has a home once #18 lands). Every entry: target nvs_namespace string, owner_description, NvsResetClassification, encryption_required, implemented_today, and a bounded (max 10) array of exact/prefix NvsKeyPattern entries.

validation_logic_implemented.detail: validate_nvs_namespace_registry() detects kDuplicateKeyClaim (two entries' key patterns could match the same real key: exact-exact, exact-inside-prefix, or overlapping prefixes) and kImplementedFlagKeyCountMismatch (implemented_today disagrees with whether any key patterns are listed) -- directly implementing the plan's own Tests-section line 'NVS namespace ownership and duplicate-key inventory'. The pairwise conflict primitive (nvs_namespace_entries_conflict) is exposed publicly so tests exercise the detection logic against synthetic conflicting entries, not just assert the shipped table happens to be clean.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: Only plan #9 (namespace ownership) and #15 (FD-21 classification) are implemented in this sub-slice; #10 (typed storage-port results), #11 (migration scaffolding), #12 (runtime encryption-verified write gate), #13 (TLS/provisioning storage interfaces), #14 (redaction), #16/#17 (actual erase/preserve enforcement) and #18 (reset-journal storage port) are not.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: The user selected 'S5 #9-18: Шифроване сховище' as a single recommended option covering the whole ten-item 'Encrypted storage foundation' cluster, but that cluster is large enough that every later item genuinely depends on the namespace registry existing first (e.g. #10's typed storage-port results need to know which namespace a call targets to decide encryption_required; #16/#17's erase enforcement needs the FD-21 classification to know what NOT to touch). Implementing the foundation first and thoroughly, rather than attempting all ten items in one shallow pass, matches this document's own established sub-slicing discipline from S5 #1-4 and #5.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: No hal_nvs.c call site has actually changed yet -- every existing NVS read/write still goes through the single hardcoded 'zigbee_gateway' namespace exactly as before this pass. The registry is a planning/classification artifact consumed by future sub-slices, not yet by any production code path. This is intentional and low-risk (pure addition, 84/84 existing tests unaffected) rather than an oversight.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: The registry's nvs_namespace field for every pre-existing entry still says the shared legacy 'zigbee_gateway' string, not a distinct real namespace per category, even though plan #9 asks for 'explicit encrypted NVS namespaces'.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Actually separating hal_nvs.c's single hardcoded namespace into multiple real ESP-IDF NVS namespaces is a live-data migration with restart-safety and power-loss implications -- explicitly plan #11's job ('Add restart-safe migration scaffolding for legacy plaintext values... No automatic migration executes until S6 authorization/physical-presence policy exists'), not something this registry sub-slice should do as a side effect.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: Until #11 lands, the registry's nvs_namespace field for pre-existing entries is aspirational/documentary (what the namespace SHOULD be once migrated) rather than descriptive of the real current ESP-IDF NVS namespace layout, which is still exactly one namespace for everything. New (implemented_today=false) entries name their intended future namespace directly since there is no existing data to migrate for them.
